sections.section_title: Initial Clinical Presentation and Immediate Assessment in Pregnancy
sections.description: This section outlines the patient’s background, presenting symptoms, and the key physical findings that guided the early differential diagnosis, emphasizing the importance of safe and rapid evaluation in a pregnant woman.
subtopics: Obstetric and demographic profile (age, BMI, parity, gestational age)
Upper abdominal and pelvic pain with dyspnea (VAS scores)
Vital signs and basic laboratory workup (CBC, CRP, urinalysis)
Physical examination of abdomen and uterus (size, tenderness, palpable masses)
Respiratory assessment (oxygen saturation, signs of diaphragmatic compression)
Initial differential: mass effect, infection, obstructive symptoms

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup in Pregnancy: Imaging and Tumor Markers
sections.description: This section details the selection and interpretation of imaging modalities safe for pregnancy, and the use of serum tumor markers, particularly the physiological behavior of CA‑125 during gestation.
subtopics: Safe imaging options (ultrasound with Doppler, non‑contrast MRI) and contraindicated modalities (CT)
Ultrasound features: unilocular cystic masses, size, peripheral vascularisation, location (subphrenic vs pouch of Douglas)
MRI characteristics: T1/T2 fat‑sat, wall thickness, focal solid components, lack of contrast enhancement
Interpretation of CA‑125 in pregnancy (physiologic peaks, significance of a rising trend)
Inclusion of other tumor markers (CA‑19‑9, CA‑15‑3, CEA, β‑2‑microglobulin, LDH)
Role of urine culture and bacterial infection in differential diagnosis

sections.section_title: Differential Diagnosis of Large Cystic Abdominal Masses in the Second Trimester
sections.description: This section presents the spectrum of possible etiologies for large cystic masses, their distinguishing imaging and laboratory features, and how they relate to the patient’s symptoms.
subtopics: Decidualised endometrioma: imaging pattern, CA‑125 trend, symptom profile
Cystic/degenerating leiomyoma: pedunculated or intramural‑subserosal, vascularised, risk of torsion/necrosis
Ovarian cystic lesions: functional, hemorrhagic, benign cystadenoma
Rare cystic entities: pseudomyxoma peritonei, Meigs syndrome, epidermoid cysts
Benign versus malignant considerations: solid components, irregular margins, tumor markers
Symptom correlation: pain, dyspnea, infection, growth rate

sections.description: This section explains the criteria for surgical intervention versus expectant management, the choice of operative approach, intra‑operative precautions, and peri‑operative care to protect both mother and fetus.
subtopics: Indications for intervention: pain, dyspnea, torsion/necrosis risk, infection, rapid growth
Choice of surgical approach: laparotomy vs laparoscopy, factors influencing decision (size, location, gestational age)
Intra‑operative considerations: fetal cardiac monitoring, blood loss control, anesthesia choice, uterine manipulation
Post‑operative management: prophylactic progesterone, targeted antibiotics, iron supplementation, transfusion thresholds
Post‑operative monitoring: obstetric visits every 3 weeks, evaluation of residual masses

sections.description: This section summarizes the maternal and neonatal outcomes, the behavior of the residual myoma, and the key lessons that can be applied to future similar cases, highlighting evidence gaps and research directions.
subtopics: Maternal outcomes: anemia resolution, infection control, residual myoma evolution, breastfeeding
Fetal outcomes: gestational age at delivery, mode of delivery, neonatal growth metrics
Residual myoma management: observed shrinkage, postpartum regression, decision to defer surgery
Clinical lessons: multidisciplinary coordination, interpretation of CA‑125, imaging guidance, timing of surgery
Evidence gaps and future research directions
